posts.pinComment: If approvals are slowing you down, comment OPS for the checklist (gates + STOP + escalation).
posts.text:
Tactical Series #16

Approval fatigue is workflow debt.

If every request looks equally urgent, teams stop assessing risk and start clicking approve to survive the queue.

Good governance is selective friction: what must be reviewed, what can auto-pass, and what escalates.

If your approval layer is slowing delivery, DM me "OPS".

posts.pinComment: Prompt changes without a registry? Comment OPS for the practical checklist.
posts.text:
Tactical Series #17

No prompt registry, no production memory.

If behavior changed and nobody can answer what changed, when, and why, your system is running on folklore.

Version + owner + risk note + rollback.

That simple.

If you need prompt governance without bureaucracy theater, DM me "OPS".

posts.pinComment: Incident playbook gaps? Comment OPS and I will send the checklist.
posts.text:
Tactical Series #18

Incidents are never "rare" the week they arrive in clusters.

Reliability is calendar reality: rotation, escalation, response window, postmortem ownership.

Agents reduce toil only when this backbone exists.

If your stack is one alert away from panic, DM me "OPS".

posts.pinComment: Fallback path design questions? Comment OPS for the framework.
posts.text:
Tactical Series #19

Fallback is product design, not a backup folder.

If your flow only works when every dependency is healthy, you shipped luck.

Design graceful degradation: what still works, what pauses safely, and what informs users clearly.

Want resilient AI workflows instead of brittle demos? DM me "OPS".

posts.pinComment: Need cleaner decision trails for agent work? Comment OPS.
posts.text:
Tactical Series #20

Decision logs compound velocity.

Without a decision trail, teams re-argue old choices every sprint and call it collaboration.

Log the decision, risk accepted, trigger for reversal, and owner.

If your team is moving fast but memory is breaking, DM me "OPS".
